why: A fourth-kind object of a chip unit's own (no support chip's: support_objects) keeps its element where its spawner stores it, BN4's +0x17 and, by the recipe's immediate for that store, BN6's +0x0E (tools/xchiprecipe_bn4.py: THUMB_STRB 0x17 -> 0xE, the object's own read of it THUMB_LDRB likewise). The trace lays a first- and a third-kind object's element out at BN6's place itself (src/dev/xdiff_bn4_trace.c obj_segs) and writes a fourth-kind object raw, so BN4's is read at BN6's place here, where BN4's +0x0E holds 0. By type, each with the two instructions.

T4.0x81: Meteors' controller: its spawner stores r3, the attack's element as BN4's misc run handed it, at +0x17 (BN4 0x080EAE80: strb r3,[r0,#0x17]) and its step reads it there for each star (0x080EAE54: ldrb r2,[r5,#0x17]); its copy's two instructions name +0x0E (src/emu/xchips_bn4.c meteors_imms). No other routine of the type (0x080EADF4-0x080EAE92) reads or writes +0x0E or +0x17. bn4_chip_meteors1 at t33: 1 at BN4's +0x17 and at BN6's +0x0E
T4.0x6c: PitRng's launcher: its spawner, a misc routine of BN4's shorter than the support routines' common one (BN4_PITRNG 0x080E9A36: movs r0,#0x6c; the spawn 0x08003344), stores r2, the attack's element, at +0x17 (0x080E9A46: strb r2,[r0,#0x17]) and its step reads it there for each boomerang (0x080E9A12: ldrb r2,[r5,#0x17]); its copy's two instructions name +0x0E (src/emu/xchips_bn4.c pitrng_imms). No other routine of the type (0x080E999C-0x080E9A50) reads or writes +0x0E or +0x17. bn4_pa_pitrng1 at t33: 4 at BN4's +0x17 and at BN6's +0x0E
